strengths: Addresses well-motivated limitations of CholecT50 with clear evidence: missing spatial annotations, inconsistent temporal boundaries, and single-source bias
Rigorous annotation methodology with >50 contributors, multiple verification phases, and clinically-grounded temporal boundary definitions (continuous vs. momentary actions)
Multi-source data from three institutions reduces single-source bias and reflects real-world variability in instruments and surgical strategies
Increased task complexity meaningfully reflects real-world surgical environments: up to 7 concurrent triplets/frame vs. CholecT50 max 3, demonstrating clinical relevance
Comprehensive evaluation with 10+ baseline methods showing clear performance gap between weak supervision (Tripnet-Det/RDV-Det: <2% mAP) and full supervision (best methods: 35% mAP)
Novel Triplet Perspective tracking annotation extends beyond standard instrument-only tracking to capture semantic evolution of surgical actions
Proper ethical considerations including IRB approval, data anonymization, informed consent, and non-commercial licensing
weaknesses: Modest absolute performance despite full supervision (F1: 31.26%, Precision/Recall: ~35%) remains far below clinical deployment thresholds, raising concerns about fundamental task solvability versus dataset difficulty
Limited algorithmic novelty: YOLO-Triplet is straightforward combination of YOLOv12 + ResNet18 + attention; primarily a data contribution with minimal methodological innovation
Insufficient scale by modern standards: only 21 videos total (14 for training) and 165K instances heavily dependent on per-video statistics; comparable datasets typically contain hundreds of videos
Long-tail distribution explicitly acknowledged but unaddressed: no proposed handling strategies, loss weighting, or sampling methods provided despite 100+ categories occurring <100 times

Missing inter-annotator agreement statistics: no Cohen's/Fleiss' kappa, reliability metrics, or formal documentation of disagreement resolution procedures; 'extremely close to' contact remains subjective
Limited cross-source generalization validation: no systematic cross-institution evaluation (train on [Our+PSI-AVA] → test on ESAD) despite multi-source advantage claims
Scope narrowly limited to single surgical procedure (robot-assisted prostatectomy only) with questionable generalization to other surgical specialties or open procedures
No systematic ablation studies demonstrating bounding box annotation value or temporal boundary impact; limited analysis of which dataset characteristics drive performance gaps

strengths: Addresses critical gap in existing datasets by providing first fully-supervised surgical triplet detection dataset with precise bounding box annotations and clinically-defined temporal boundaries
Rigorous annotation process with strong inter-rater agreement (Kappa=0.82), clinical supervision, and 60+ contributors including practicing surgeons
Comes with valuable practical contributions beyond the dataset: two novel open-source annotation tools (Triplet-labelme, SurgLabel) and enhanced evaluation toolkit (ivtdmetrics)
Multi-institutional composition (21 videos from 3 sources) increases credibility and reflects real-world surgical variability
Increased task complexity compared to CholecT50 (prostatectomy vs cholecystectomy with 58.77% frames having ≥3 concurrent instances vs 6.75%)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation: 14 methods benchmarked, 5-fold cross-validation, multiple protocols (frame-wise and video-wise), detailed per-class analysis
Strong reproducibility with detailed implementations, extensive appendices (32 pages), and clear data release plans
Baseline method (TDnet) demonstrates novel instance-level self-distillation approach for addressing class imbalance in surgical tasks
weaknesses: Limited to single surgical procedure (RARP only), reducing scope and generalizability compared to multi-procedure datasets; transferability of tools to other procedures unclear
Fewer unique procedures than prior work (21 videos vs 50 in CholecT50), which may limit model generalization across different surgeon styles and institutional practices
Severe class imbalance remains largely unresolved: baseline achieves only 36.1% mAP@0.5 for full triplets and 32.8% F1-score, suggesting task remains far from solved despite the dataset
Temporal information provided in annotations is not effectively utilized: Appendix G.2 shows temporal modules yielded 'limited results' and sometimes worse performance than frame-wise baselines

Low absolute performance metrics (34.7% precision, 39.7% recall, many high confusion rates) raise questions about practical clinical deployment feasibility without addressing error severity or clinical implications
Baseline method shows only marginal improvements over YOLOv12 (1.8% at mAP@0.5, 1.3% at mAP@0.5:0.95) despite added architectural complexity; limited algorithmic novelty
Inter-rater agreement validated on only 5 surgeons across 5 non-overlapping segments (1000 frames); no cross-annotator group comparison or temporal consistency analysis
Dataset composition is imbalanced across sources: PWH (41.3%), PSI-AVA (36.3%), ESAD (22.4%), potentially biasing models toward PWH characteristics with no stratification analysis
Re-annotation strategy discards existing annotations from ESAD and PSI-AVA rather than leveraging them, increasing effort but potentially introducing systematic biases; impact not analyzed

Incomplete baseline comparisons: weak-supervision methods perform at near-zero levels (not meaningful comparison), CholecQ dismissed without quantitative analysis, no cross-dataset transfer learning evaluation
